content: 1. Topiramate increases sedation when co-administered with certain drugs. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 2. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of estradiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 3. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of esterified estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is recommended, and close monitoring is required. 5. Topiramate may compromise the efficacy of estrogens used in contraception or hormone replacement therapies. Close monitoring is essential. 6. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Co-administration of eszopiclone and topiramate increases sedation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 8. Ethanol and topiramate both increase sedation. Ethanol increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 9. Ether increases the toxicity of phentermine through an unknown mechanism, posing risks of ventricular tachycardia (V-tach) and hypertension (HTN). Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 11. Topiramate increases the levels of ethotoin by decreasing its metabolism, while ethotoin decreases topiramate levels by increasing its metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown; monitor closely. 12. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 14. Eucalyptus and topiramate both increase sedation. Eucalyptus increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 15. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of everolimus via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of felodipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Fenfluramine and phentermine both increase sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as elevated blood pressure and heart rate. Topiramate increases sedation, while fenfluramine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 19. Fentanyl and topiramate both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of fesoterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of finasteride via CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Fluoxetine and phentermine increase each other's toxicity through an unknown mechanism, posing a risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Fluphenazine and topiramate both increase sedation. Fluphenazine increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 25. Fluvoxamine and phentermine both increase serotonin levels, posing a risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Formoterol and phentermine both increase sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as elevated blood pressure and heart rate. Topiramate increases sedation, while formoterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 27. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Fosphenytoin decreases topiramate levels by increasing its metabolism, while topiramate increases fosphenytoin levels by decreasing its metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown; monitor closely. 30. Topiramate and ganaxolone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of glyburide through an unknown mechanism. The impact on glycemic control is likely small. 32. Green tea may contain caffeine, a CNS stimulant, which can have additive effects when combined with other CNS stimulants. Avoid or use caffeine cautiously. 33. Guarana increases the effects of phentermine through pharmacodynamic synergy. The significance of this interaction is unknown; monitor closely. 34. Haloperidol increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. Haloperidol and topiramate both increase sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 35. Sympathomimetics can antagonize the activity of some antihypertensive agents, such as hydralazine. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Hydromorphone and topiramate both increase sedation. Hydromorphone increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 38. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Hydroxyzine increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. Hydroxyzine and topiramate both increase sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 40. Iloperidone and topiramate both increase sedation. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of iloperidone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 41. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Imipramine and topiramate both increase sedation. Imipramine increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 43. Tricyclic antidepressants, such as imipramine, can increase or decrease the effects of sympathomimetics by blocking norepinephrine reuptake or uptake of indirect sympathomimetics into adrenergic neurons. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of indinavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Phentermine decreases the effects of iobenguane I-123 by receptor binding competition, potentially causing false-negative imaging results. Discontinue interfering drugs for at least five half-lives before administration. 46. Phentermine reduces the levels or effects of iobenguane I-131. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Drugs that reduce catecholamine uptake or deplete catecholamine stores may interfere with iobenguane uptake into cells, reducing its efficacy. Discontinue interfering drugs for at least five half-lives before administration. 48. Phentermine decreases the effects of ioflupane I-123 by receptor binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Isocarboxazid increases the effects of phentermine through pharmacodynamic synergy, posing a risk of acute hypertensive episodes. This combination is contraindicated. 51. Isoflurane increases the toxicity of phentermine through an unknown mechanism, posing risks of V-tach and HTN. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Isoproterenol and phentermine both decrease sedation. Topiramate increases sedation, while isoproterenol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 53. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of isradipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole via CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Ketamine and topiramate both increase sedation. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 56. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of ketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Ketotifen (ophthalmic) and topiramate both increase sedation. Ketotifen increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 58. Topiramate increases the toxicity of lacosamide. Co-administration with sodium channel-blocking antiseizure drugs may increase the risk of AV block, bradycardia, or ventricular tachyarrhythmias. Monitor ECG before and after titration. 59. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of lapatinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Lasmiditan and topiramate both increase sedation. Co-administration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated in clinical studies. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Lemborexant increases the levels or effects of topiramate by sedation. Dosage adjustment may be necessary when co-administered with other CNS depressants due to potentially additive effects. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 62. Topiramate increases sedation, while levalbuterol decreases it. Levalbuterol and phentermine both increase sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as elevated blood pressure and heart rate. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 63. Levetiracetam and topiramate both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Topiramate decreases the levels of levocarnitine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 65. Levocetirizine and topiramate both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 67. Levomilnacipran and phentermine both increase serotonin levels, posing a risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 68. Topiramate decreases the levels of levonorgestrel (intrauterine or oral) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; alternative or backup contraception is recommended. 70. Levorphanol increases sedation, while phentermine decreases it. Levorphanol and topiramate both increase sedation. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 71. Topiramate increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is administered with a CYP3A4 inducer. 72. Linezolid increases the effects of phentermine, posing a risk of serotonin syndrome. This combination is contraindicated.
